title: Context-sensitive ion channels appear alongside complex metazoan body plans

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Context-sensitive ion channels appear alongside complex metazoan body plans

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Ion channel phylogeny is ancient (many channel families likely predate the most recent unicellular ancestor of animals), and the appearance of context-sensitive channels enabling new bioelectric feedback loops tracks the appearance of complex body plans at the emergence of metazoa, indicating an evolutionary continuum from single-cell excitability to cognition via somatic pattern control.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The phylogeny of ion channels is ancient, and the appearance of context-sensitive channels (enabling new kinds of bioelectrical feedback loops) tracks well with the appearance of complex body plans at the emergence of metazoa (Moran et al., 2015), revealing the remarkable evolutionary continuum that leads from membrane excitability in single cells to cognitive functions in advanced organisms, by way of somatic pattern control (Cook et al., 2014).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems”. Scope: Ion channel gene families across unicellular eukaryotes and early-branching metazoans

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-26: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public comparative resources can robustly test channel antiquity and temporal association with metazoan diversification. The functional and cognitive interpretation remains underdetermined, making the full claim only partially resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Date duplications and domain innovations in context-sensitive ion-channel families on a species tree, then test their association with independently coded body-plan complexity while controlling phylogeny and genome quality.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Gene loss and poor early-branching genomes bias ancestral reconstruction.

Body-plan complexity and context sensitivity require subjective coding.

Correlation does not establish the proposed continuum to cognition.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Channel-family presence across choanoflagellates, sponges, ctenophores, and cnidarians can be rebuilt from public orthology and domain databases with a standard phylogenetic presence-absence analysis. That tests whether context-sensitive families appear with metazoan complexity, within the limits of domain-based classification. It does not test the claimed continuum onward to cognition.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Build a presence-absence matrix of voltage- and ligand-gated channel families across unicellular eukaryotes and early metazoans and test whether context-sensitive families originate at the metazoan node, alongside gains in body-plan complexity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Channel gains at the origin of animals coincide with many other novelties, so a correlation does not isolate body-plan complexity.

The further continuum from excitability through somatic patterning to cognition is not in these matrices.

Domain presence is an imperfect stand-in for context-sensitive gating.
